text:
jen: Quick follow-up on dashboard render perf. noticed a lot of repeated RBAC lookups when pages render 20+ widgets. spike in CPU and auth service QPS. thinking about an "auth aggregation" shim in the gateway that dedups identical checks within a short window and evaluates them lazily.

hafsa: can you sketch how "dedup" differs from the existing cache? i assume this groups by (subject, resource, action) per-render and returns a single proto-decision to all waiters?

jen: exactly. difference: cache is long-lived (per-tenant TTL) while aggregation is ephemeral and tied to a render id / debounce window (10-30ms). it avoids hammering auth backends for the same simultaneous widget checks.

mike: sounds promising. main tradeoffs i see: increased p99 for first widget if aggregation waits, risk of head-of-line blocking if aggregation backend stalls, and memory for holding waiter lists during the window.

jen: agreed. mitigation ideas: 1) short window (default 20ms), 2) priority lanes (interactive routes bypass or parallel execute), 3) cap waiters per-key (e.g., 64) and fall back to async-fire-and-cache if exceeded.

nate: op concern: tenant isolation. if we aggregate globally we must shard by tenant and not let one tenant's busy dashboard cause cross-tenant memory pressure. also enforce per-tenant entry caps.

hafsa: revocation model? if a permission revokes mid-window we must not incorrectly allow. but since window is tiny we can rely on revocation stream to invalidate cache; aggregation must consult the same revocation stream before answering if the key was invalidated in-flight.

jen: sketch config (gateway):

```yaml
auth_aggregation:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 20
  max_waiters_per_key: 64
  per_tenant_entry_limit: 1024
  high_priority_routes: [ "/console/render", "/console/live" ]
  fallback_strategy: "direct-check"  # options: direct-check | async-cache | fail-open
```

mike: metrics we need: agg_requests_total, agg_hit_ratio, agg_waiters_histogram, agg_fallback_count, agg_latency_by_route. also gauge for current_agg_entries and per_tenant_entry_count. add audit log entries for aggregated decisions so we can trace auth flows.

nate: add circuit-breaker hook: if auth backend latency > X or error rate spikes, turn off aggregation for affected tenants to avoid long waits. simple kill-switch per-region/tenant.

hafsa: rollout plan: 1) internal dogfood with console team (non-prod) 2) opt-in tenant flag for Dedicated/Private 3) 1% hosted canary for low-traffic tenants 4) widen with SLO guardrails.

jen: SLO guardrail proposal:
- median render auth path latency delta <= 8ms
- p95 delta <= 20ms
- p999 delta <= 80ms (auto rollback)
- no auth-errors increase > 0.1% absolute

mike: compatibility: add header X-Auth-Aggregation: off to bypass per-route or for dashboards using inline behavior. document consoles that rely on side-effect ordering.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: gateway/auth-agg v0.1 -> tag: agg-canary-2026-03-22; expires in 14d

nate: followups: 1) write a short RFC follow-up with microbenchmarks and memory model, 2) implement simple in-memory waiter map + eviction, 3) test revocation stream integration in staging.

jen: i'll draft the follow-up today and ping reviewers. thanks for the quick inputs. :rocket:
